latest.title: Highly Positive Geophysics Results from Monal
latest.content:
20 Aug 2026 07:00
RNS Number : 4003R
Mila Resources PLC
20 August 2026
Mila Resources Plc / Index: LSE / Epic: MILA / Sector: Natural Resources
20 August 2026
Mila Resources Plc
("Mila" or the "Company")
Highly Positive Geophysics Results from Monal Copper-Gold Project:
Compelling Drill Targets for Potential Epithermal & Porphyry Cu-Au Mineralisation
Mila Resources Plc (LSE: MILA), the post-discovery gold and copper resource development company focused on Australia, is pleased to announce highly positive results of Induced Polarisation (IP) surveys at key targets at the Company's 100% owned Monal Copper-Gold Project in south-eastern Queensland ("Monal" or the "Project").
This IP programme builds on extensive work completed by the Company since acquiring the Project, including the review of historic exploration data, geological mapping and surface sampling. The integration of this new geophysical dataset with existing geological and geochemical information presents clear drill targets for potential epithermal and porphyry copper, gold and molybdenum mineralisation.
Highlights
Basilica Prospect:
·
Three dipole-dipole IP lines have been surveyed and modelled across the Basilica and Jazza targets (7282700N, 7282850N, 7283000N), all confirmed to good data quality (n ≥ 18, strong reciprocity, ~300 m depth of investigation).
·
Results show a clear target between 200 to 300m, with the porphyry characteristics of a chargeability halo surrounding a deep resistivity low that itself becomes conductive with depth, interpreted as a potential sulphide-bearing zone around a more altered core (shown in Figure 1).
·
Rock chip sampling returned high-grade Cu-Au-Ag assays at surface, hosted in quartz veins with visible chalcopyrite and pyrite, directly above the chargeability anomaly. The technical team considers the veins to be a possible surface expression of this deeper anomaly, consistent with a porphyry-style target at depth.
·
Latest rock chips from quartz veins with visible sulphides returned results up to 0.72 g/t Au, 1.77% Cu and 51 g/t Ag, and historic reports list rock chip samples of up to 2% Cu and 2.34 g/t from sulphidic quartz veins in the same area
Childs Prospect:
·
Porphyry-like characteristics demonstrated, with gradient-array IP results defining a compact, high-amplitude chargeability high with a closed, ring-shaped signature, coincident with a resistivity low - a pairing consistent with a discrete buried source.
·
A historic nearby auger hole returned coincident copper-gold-molybdenum values, with elevated copper geochemistry more broadly in the wider area.
·
The Childs prospect lies approximately 10 km NNE of the Mount Cannindah deposit (JORC MRE 14.5Mt @ 1.09% CuEq) within the same regional structural corridor.
Commenting, Executive Director Mark Stephenson said:
"The results from our work at Monal are showing scale, having followed up on historic work and finding extensive surface expressions of copper, gold and molybdenum; the team is extremely encouraged. The IP results, together with rock chip sampling showing clear porphyry-style signatures at surface, have significantly strengthened our view of the Project's potential for multiple yet undefined near-surface porphyries across the wider licence area.
"The combination of compelling drill targets within a proven mineralised district highlights the opportunity at Monal and adds meaningful value to Mila's wider Queensland portfolio.
"We are particularly excited by the scale and quality of the targets now emerging and intend to advance them. These results further demonstrate the depth and quality of Mila's broader asset base and the potential for multiple projects to deliver substantial value for shareholders."
FURTHER INFORMATION
Regional Context
The Monal Project lies within the Yarrol Province of the New England Orogen, a major orogenic belt hosting numerous porphyry Cu-Au-Mo and skarn-mineralised corridors. Within the Yarrol Province, key regional analogues include Mount Cannindah, the large Briggs porphyry Cu-Mo system, and the Coalstoun Lakes Cu-Au-Mo porphyry, demonstrating the fertility of the local intrusive suites.
The Basilica and Childs Prospects together with several historically-worked occurrences, are distributed around the margins of the Late Triassic Glassford Complex. Basilica and Childs sit approximately 21 km apart on the western and eastern sides of the complex respectively, with the historically worked Blue Bag-Lady Inez Cu-Fe skarns lying between them (15 km east of Basilica, 6 km west of Childs). Basilica additionally lies 4 km SSE of the Silver Star-Munholme Creek occurrence, on the complex's western margin. Childs lies approximately 10 km NNE of the Mount Cannindah deposit.
This concentration of known porphyry systems and mineralised occurrences around the Glassford Complex provides strong regional support for the Company's interpretation of Monal as prospective for a significant porphyry-related Cu-Au-Mo mineral system.
Basilica Prospect
·
Rock chips collected by Mila from quartz veins with visible sulphides returned results up to 0.72 g/t Au, 1.77 % Cu and 51 g/t Ag.
·
Historic reports list rock chip samples of up to 2 % Cu and 2.34 g/t from sulphidic quartz veins.
·
A chargeability halo surrounds a deep resistivity low that itself becomes conductive with depth, interpreted as a sulphide-bearing zone around a more altered core.
·
Full-resolution RL depth slices (+557 to +317) show this response tightening into a coherent, closing feature at depth rather than remaining diffuse or open - consistent with a genuine pipe-like body rather than a survey-edge artefact.
·
A circular ground magnetic low is coincident with the IP response at the RL317 slice. This rules out magnetite as the source of the chargeability and instead supports magnetite-destructive (phyllic) alteration - a well-documented, diagnostic porphyry-halo signature.
Figure
1
. Modelled IP results at the Basilica target. Pink polygon shows a high chargeability zone overlying a more resistive core and capped by a resistive zone above. Mineralised quartz veins were sampled at surface around this feature.
Figure
2
. Material sampled for rock chips in the Basilica Prospect targets. (L) Mineralised quartz vein outcropping at Basilica and (R) sulphide-rich material at Eastern Star.
Childs prospect
·
Legacy soil geochemistry indicates a zoned multi-element signature around the IP anomaly, with alteration-style geochemistry proximal to the anomaly grading outward into a discrete copper-gold-silver soil anomaly (to 381 ppm Cu) approximately 250 m east. A single shallow auger hole 570 m away separately returned coincident copper-gold-molybdenum values (384 ppm Cu, 0.18 g/t Au, 1.8 ppm Mo)
·
The prospect lies along a NE-SW trending lineament, 2km NE of the established Boggy Creek Au prospect containing a mineralised diorite intrusive and 10km NNE of Mt Cannindah
·
Interpreted as a circular intrusive related structure from magnetic and photogeological interpretation.
·
Recent Gradient Array IP surveying over 4.2 km² has defined a broadly NNW-trending anomaly fabric across the survey area, with strong resistivity highs concentrated in the eastern blocks and numerous chargeability highs distributed through the western blocks.
·
A compelling high-amplitude chargeability high with a closed, ring-shaped signature, coincident with a resistivity low suggests a buried intrusive source, similar to the Basilica target within the western part of the survey grid.
Rock Chip Assays
Sampling of veins and gossanous material at the Basilica Prospect targets returned excellent copper, gold and silver grades. Anomalous grades for Mo, Bi, Pb and Zn were also found in several samples.

latest.title: Queensland Exploration Programme & Drilling Update
latest.content:
17 Aug 2026 10:30
RNS Number : 9577Q
Mila Resources PLC
17 August 2026
Mila Resources Plc / Index: LSE / Epic: MILA / Sector: Natural Resources
17 August 2026
Mila Resources Plc
(“Mila” or the “Company”)
Queensland Exploration Programme Update
& Drilling to Re-commence
Drilling targeting the extension and infill of gold mineralisation across the 20km Yarrol System
Mila Resources Plc (LSE: MILA), the post-discovery gold and copper resource development company focused on Australia, is pleased to announce an update on its exploration programme across its 100% owned gold and copper portfolio in Queensland, Australia.
HIGHLIGHTS
Mila’s fully funded 1,400m drilling campaign in Queensland is now underway.
New phase of drilling will build on the ~5,000 metres of drilling completed by the Company to date at the Yarrol Gold Project (“Yarrol”).
Drilling to date has confirmed the scale and continuity of the gold system at Yarrol and has demonstrated that mineralisation remains open in multiple directions – previous intercepts include:
24m @ 29.4g/t Au from 8m including 1m @ 112g/t
17m @ 5.47g/t Au from 42m including 1m @ 47.4g/t
9m @ 2.48g/t Au from 31m including 1m @ 15.05g/t
New campaign will comprise nine holes targeting depths of up to 200 metres, testing extensions to known and new mineralisation targets
Work has been refined by AI-generated target ranking and drilling optimised work along the Yarrol Fault system.
Drill targets informed by MINML's AI-integrated geoscience platform, which ranked prospective targets using Mila's geological interpretations and historical exploration datasets.
Latest drilling programme is one element of the Company’s staged exploration strategy across its portfolio of gold and copper projects in Queensland, including the delineation of a Mineral Resource Estimate (“MRE”) and delivery of preliminary economic studies at Yarrol.
Mark Stephenson, Executive Director of Mila, commented:
“It has been four months, and our team are now back drilling in Queensland.
In that time, we have seen a step change in our understanding of the Yarrol deposit and now even more confident in the scale of this system.
“Recent AI work by MinML has supported our work, ensuring we have a stronger understanding of the system’s mineral controlling structures, and incorporating geophysical analysis to help rank target generation.
“With all of this information at hand, we set the team a challenge: with the metres budgeted, balance conservative resource definition work without compromising blue sky scale of this system.
The result is a programme that is well designed to extend our understanding of the gold system and to test the most prospective targets identified to date.
“Investors can look forward to a busy period of news flow as assay results come through in the weeks ahead and as we continue our pre-resource evaluation and preliminary economic phases at Yarrol, with the objective of delivering a commercially and technically compelling development prospect over the coming months.”
Figure 1. Overview of Mila completed drill programmes at Yarrol and upcoming drill programme.
Objective of the Drilling Programme
This latest programme comprises nine drill holes for a total of 1,400 metres, targeting depths of up to 200 metres. The programme is designed to infill and extend known mineralisation, test new AI-generated targets along strike, and provide data to support an updated MRE.
As announced on 3 August 2026, Mila engaged London-based AI geoscience specialist MINML to integrate machine learning into target generation for the Yarrol programme. MINML's platform has ranked exploration targets by integrating geological, geophysical and geochemical datasets and calibrating its models against Mila's geological interpretations and historical data. The drill programme incorporates these AI-assisted targets alongside geologically defined objectives.
​
Figure 2. Overview of the entire Yarrol project area showing the Yarrol Fault and the small section tested to date.
Q4 Programme
During Q4 2026, the Company plans a multi-pronged work programme across its Yarrol and Monal projects aimed at advancing both near-term resource growth and longer-term exploration upside. At Yarrol, metallurgical test work will be carried out on key ore zones to build a clearer picture of processing characteristics, running alongside updated geological and resource modelling as the project progresses towards a maiden or updated resource estimate. This will be complemented by drilling of new targets along the Yarrol fault corridor, designed to test the extent of mineralisation and demonstrate the project's potential for further resource growth beyond the current footprint. At Monal, the Company will continue to advance its target inventory through additional geological mapping and geophysical surveys, sharpening the definition of priority drill targets, with scout drilling planned at the most promising of these to test their potential ahead of a possible follow-up campaign.
FURTHER INFORMATION
The Yarrol Gold Project is located in Queensland, Australia, along the Yarrol Fault, a major structural corridor extending over 20 km. Mila's exploration programme to date, comprising approximately 5,000 metres of drilling together with geological mapping, geochemical interpretation and geophysical analysis, has confirmed the continuity of gold mineralisation and its extension beyond the footprint of the historic Yarrol North resource, while demonstrating that the system remains open along strike and at depth.

latest.title: Mila moves to 100% Ownership in Queensland
latest.content:
12 Aug 2026 07:00
RNS Number : 2484Q
Mila Resources PLC
12 August 2026
Mila Resources Plc / Index: LSE / Epic: MILA / Sector: Natural Resources
12 August 2026
Mila Resources Plc
("Mila" or the "Company")
Mila moves to 100% Ownership in Queensland
Mila Resources Plc (LSE: MILA), the post-discovery gold and copper resource development company focused on Australia, is pleased to announce that in accordance with the announcement of 31 October 2024, it has now completed the exercise of the EMX Option Agreement ("EMX Option Agreement") with EMX Royalty Corp ("EMX") (and subsequently became Elemental Royalty Corporation) following compliance and regulatory approvals in Australia.
As a result, Mila is now the 100% owner of three project areas in Queensland, Australia: Yarrol (EPM8402, EPM27561, EPM28230 and EPM28658), Mount Steadman (EPM12834 and EPM27750) and Mount Weary, which encompasses the Monal Gold-Copper Project (EPM26317 and EPM27252) (collectively the "Exploration Portfolio" shown in Figure 1).
In accordance with the terms of the EMX Option Agreement, the Company shall issue EMX with 7,096,774 new ordinary shares being £110,000 of new Mila ordinary shares ("Option Fee Shares") valued by reference to the volume weighted average price of the Company's listed shares during thirty consecutive trading days ending on 30 October 2025 ("30 Day VWAP") of 1.55 pence per share.
The Option Fee Shares issued to EMX are subject to a lock up for twelve months from the date of admission to trading.
Admission and Total Voting Rights
An application has been made for the Option Fee Shares to be admitted to trading on the Official List and the London Stock Exchange with effect from 8.00 a.m. on 17 August 2026 ("Admission").
In accordance with the FCA's Disclosure Guidance and Transparency Rules, the Company confirms that following Admission, the Company's enlarged issued ordinary share capital will comprise 744,657,696 Ordinary Shares. The Company does not hold any Ordinary Shares in Treasury. Therefore, following Admission, the above figure may be used by shareholders in the Company as the denominator for the calculations to determine if they are required to notify their interest in, or a change to their interest in the Company, under the FCA's Disclosure Guidance and Transparency Rules.
Mark Stephenson, Executive Chairman commented:
"We are delighted to have 100% ownership of the Yarrol, Mount Steadman and Mount Weary exploration portfolio in Queensland and we have also now set up our subsidiary in Australia.
"This is an important milestone for Mila, providing the Company with full ownership and control of a highly prospective portfolio of gold and copper exploration assets. We are very busy pulling together our next phase of work at Yarrol with drilling imminent and our regional work continues to deliver further evidence of high-quality targets. We'll be entering a highly active period in the forthcoming months and look forward to sharing that with the shareholders."

latest.title: Target Generation & Next Phase of Drilling
latest.content:
3 Aug 2026 07:00
RNS Number : 9513O
Mila Resources PLC
03 August 2026
Mila Resources Plc / Index: LSE / Epic: MILA / Sector: Natural Resources
3 August 2026
Mila Resources Plc
("Mila" or the "Company")
Target Generation and Next Phase of Drilling at Yarrol Gold Project
Mila Resources Plc (LSE: MILA), the post-discovery gold and copper resource development company focused on Australia, is pleased to announce that target generation, supported by machine learning, is now underway for the next phase of drilling at its Yarrol Gold Project in Queensland.
The next phase of drilling will build on the ~5,000-metres of drilling completed by Mila to date, which consistently demonstrated the scale and continuity of the Yarrol gold system, while also confirming that mineralisation remains open in multiple directions. This, together with an extensive review of historical exploration data and comprehensive geological studies, significantly enhanced the Company's understanding of the Yarrol mineralised system and has laid the foundation for the upcoming programme, which will be used to assess the broader scale potential of the Yarrol Gold Project beyond the established mineral resource area.
Highlights
·
Mila has partnered with London-based artificial intelligence geoscience specialist MINML to integrate machine learning into target generation to support the technical team across the Yarrol Project.
·
MINML has calibrated its machine learning platform using Mila's geological interpretations developed over the last 18 months together with historical exploration datasets.
·
Mila will use this updated, detailed model to delineate multiple targets beyond the 1 km of strike already tested and realise potential for more mineralised bodies to be found along the 20 km fault.
·
The upcoming drill programme will use the optimised deposit model to infill and test further extensions to mineralisation at Yarrol. These will be used together with further technical studies, as Mila builds towards an updated Mineral Resource Estimate ("MRE").
·
Alastair Goodship, Chief Operating Officer, is currently on site to oversee final target selection, drill preparations and commencement of the (1,400 m) funded programme.
·
Interpretation of the recently completed induced polarisation ("IP") geophysical surveys of copper targets at the Monal Licences is progressing, with a further update to be provided shortly.
Advancing the Geological Model at Yarrol
The Company's exploration programme to date has significantly advanced its understanding of the geological architecture controlling gold mineralisation at Yarrol. Through a combination of drilling, geological mapping, geochemical interpretation and geophysical analysis, Mila has developed an increasingly robust geological model defining the structural controls on mineralisation and the relationships between lithology, alteration, geochemistry and gold distribution.
The Q1 2026 drilling programme confirmed the continuity of mineralisation and its extensions to greater depths, with several drill holes intersecting multiple gold-bearing zones that collectively define broad mineralised corridors. The programme also identified multiple high-grade gold shoots from shallow depths within a large mineralised system, surrounded by a broad lower-grade halo that demonstrates the potential for significant tonnage.
Importantly, continuity of mineralisation has now been confirmed well beyond the footprint of the historic Yarrol North resource, while the system remains open along strike and at depth. Additional high-grade targets and parallel mineralised structures remain untested, highlighting considerable potential for further resource growth.
The Company's growing geological confidence also provides the foundation for future mineral resource updates. However, given the significant exploration success achieved beyond the historic resource footprint, Mila believes there is considerable value in continuing to strategically expand and upgrade the resource through targeted drilling as part of a staged development strategy.
Artificial Intelligence Assisted Target Generation
To support the next stage of exploration, Mila has engaged MINML, a London-based AI-integrated geoscience company specialising in the application of deep learning technologies to mineral exploration.
MINML has calibrated its machine learning platform using Mila's geological interpretations together with historical exploration datasets.
The initial programme has:
·
Integrated multiple geological, geophysical and geochemical datasets;
·
Identified exploration patterns associated with known mineralisation;
·
Generated ranked exploration targets;
·
Provided geological explanations supporting each identified target.
Importantly, the Company notes that MINML's approach is not a "black box" system, with all outputs linked back to geological controls that can be independently reviewed and validated by Mila's technical team.
Following the successful completion of the initial evaluation, Mila intends to incorporate this technology into the wider Yarrol exploration programme.
Exploration Strategy
The Company's exploration strategy is designed to balance near-term resource growth with the longer-term objective of unlocking the full scale of the Yarrol Gold Project.
The substantial increase in geological understanding achieved through recent drilling has demonstrated that mineralisation extends well beyond the limits of the historic resource area. As a result, the Company intends to pursue a dual-track exploration strategy, continuing to systematically grow confidence in the existing mineralised footprint while simultaneously evaluating the broader district-scale opportunity presented by the Yarrol Fault system.
This approach is expected to provide a series of technical and exploration milestones, progressively de-risking the project while maximising the opportunity to define a materially larger gold system over time.
Stage 1 - Resource Growth and Definition
Drilling will initially focus on areas where additional drilling has the potential to increase geological confidence, extend known mineralisation and support future resource updates. This work is intended to progressively enhance the quality and scale of the existing resource inventory while maintaining disciplined capital allocation.
The initial programme will focus on extending known mineralisation through:
·
Refinement of existing geological interpretations;
·
Testing strike extensions;
·
Testing depth extensions beneath known mineralisation;
·
Optimising drill orientations.
Stage 2 - District Stage Growth
In parallel with Stage 1, the Company will continue testing the broader Yarrol Fault system, applying its evolving geological model and machine-learning-assisted targeting to evaluate the considerable exploration potential beyond the currently defined mineralised footprint.
The second phase will evaluate the broader Yarrol mineral system by:
·
Applying the Company's geological model across the wider Yarrol Fault corridor;
·
Reviewing historical prospects that received limited follow-up exploration;
·
Testing previously untested geophysical and geochemical anomalies.
Monal Copper Targets Update
Interpretation of the recently completed IP geophysical surveys at the Basilica/Jazza and Childs targets in the Monal Licences is progressing, with a further update to be provided following shortly.
The survey has been designed to improve understanding of potential mineralised structures and assist in generating priority drill targets.
Commenting, Executive Director Mark Stephenson said:
"The successful application of MINML's AI-integrated geoscience platform represents another important step in advancing our understanding of the Yarrol gold system. By integrating multiple geological datasets, the programme has identified and ranked new exploration targets while, crucially, providing the geological rationale behind each recommendation. This detailed model will be used to delineate multiple targets beyond the 1km of strike already tested and realise potential for more mineralised bodies to be found along the 20km fault.
"The success of recent drilling has strengthened our confidence not only in the continuity of the existing mineralisation, but also in the scale of the wider system. Our strategy is therefore twofold: to continue building geological confidence and progressively grow the resource in the near term, whilst simultaneously testing the broader exploration opportunity that we believe has the potential to deliver substantially greater long-term value.
"This staged approach allows us to allocate capital efficiently, generate multiple exploration and resource milestones, and progressively de-risk what we believe is emerging as a significant gold system."

company_30s.what_they_do: Mila Gold is a junior Australian mining company that explores for and develops gold deposits, mainly in the Yarrol area. It focuses on drilling, resource definition and building a scalable gold system.
company_30s.why_they_matter: Gold remains a key hedge for investors and a staple in industrial alloys. Mila’s Yarrol project claims a continuous gold system, which could turn a small exploration asset into a cash‑generating mine if proven. The company’s potential lies in unlocking a sizeable, high‑grade gold resource in a country with a strong mining framework.
company_30s.current_state: The company is still in the exploration phase, generating cash through placements and management options. It is not yet producing revenue and is burning cash while building its drilling programme. The share price sits at a very low level, reflecting the high risk and long horizon typical of junior miners.

rns_narrative: The latest announcements show a steady stream of drilling results from Yarrol, including high‑grade gold intercepts and confirmation that the deposit behaves like a continuous gold system. That suggests the geology is working as expected and the company is moving closer to a mineable resource.

Funding activity is a second theme – the company has taken a £600,000 placing and has management share options that could bring in additional capital. These moves indicate the board is actively raising cash to keep the project alive.

A third thread is corporate housekeeping: management share options, an IP survey, and a series of interim results. These signals show the company is maintaining compliance and transparency, which can reassure investors that the project is being managed responsibly.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: Bullish optimism tinged with caution – traders see a potential turnaround but are wary of the long timeline.
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: Some investors point to the 11‑bagger story of a peer and the high‑grade intercepts as proof that the project could become a real gold producer. They expect the next drill results to push the price up.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Others argue the company is over‑valued for an exploration asset, that the gold system could be over‑optimistic, and that the company may run out of cash before turning a profit.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: The chatter has moved from pure skepticism to a mix of hope and hesitation. While early posts were flat, recent comments about the drill results have injected a little optimism, but the overall tone remains cautious.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends for the ticker is flat – no public interest is building, which is a good sign for a contrarian play.

near_term_catalysts: A drill report due next month that confirms more high‑grade intercepts – this would give the market a clear, data‑driven reason to move the price up.
Completion of the £600,000 placing and any subsequent capital raise – fresh cash can fund further drilling and keep the project alive.
A positive IP survey outcome for the Monal Au‑Cu project – this could broaden the company’s resource base and add upside.
expect_next.watch_for: Look for a sustained volume spike coupled with a breakout above the current support level. A clear move above the 20‑day moving average would also signal a shift in sentiment.
expect_next.timing_regime: The share is deep in a crash bottom, likely at the early stage of capitulation. If the next drill result confirms a continuous system, the mean‑reversion cycle could begin. The APEX score (high) suggests the price is under compression and ready to spring.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: The company sits in a deep crash zone – a 70‑95% drop from its peak. With a confirmed gold system and fresh capital, the price could climb back to roughly half of its pre‑crash level. That would be a 100%+ return on the current price, which is in line with the historical performance of deep‑crash signals (average >150%).
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: The main risks are that the gold system may not be as continuous as claimed, or that the company runs out of cash before it can drill enough to prove the resource. In that scenario the share could stay near its current level or drop further if a delisting or bankruptcy becomes a real threat.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Potential upside is large – a 2‑3× return is realistic if the next drill results are strong. The downside is limited to the current price because the share is already at a very low point; a 10‑20% drop would be the worst short‑term scenario.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter after a confirmed breakout above the 20‑day moving average with at least a 25% increase in daily volume. Use a 15% stop below the breakout level to protect against a false move.
playbook.if_watching: Hold cash until the next drill report is released. If the report confirms a continuous gold system, consider a quick entry. If the report is weak, stay out until a new catalyst appears.
playbook.if_passing: There are no imminent terminal risks such as delisting or bankruptcy. The primary risk is a weak drill result; if that occurs, consider exiting or tightening the stop.

ai_insights.bottom_line: Mila Gold is in a deep crash; a strong drill result next month could trigger a mean‑reversion bounce with upside exceeding 2× the current price, making it a high‑reward contrarian play.
